doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Jump Town and the Ventura band
title: How 'I'm Forever Blowing Bubbles' was chosen
summary: Ventura's manager suggests the corny tune; Roy puts it in four-four and it becomes a big record.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What made you choose, back then, “I’m Forever Blowing Bubbles?” Or any tune like that, that you wouldn’t connect—

It’s a funny one. We’re doing these things with Charlie Ventura. His manager said, “let’s take a song that everybody knows, that everybody’s heard all their lives, and do something to it so they know what different treatment we use to do that song.” So he says, “how about ‘I’m Forever Blowing Bubbles?’”
And we said oh God, no. We thought that’s such a corny tune. Even though everybody knows it and it’s a fun thing, but I mean— © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
So he says, “no, try it, see what you can come up with.” So I put it in the four-four and that was it.
That was a big record for us.
